summary: A [National AI Strategy 2026-2030](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) was approved by Cabinet in October 2025 and launched by the President in March 2026, and the strategy text is now held in full.
developments:
Trade press reported six pillars where the document sets out four strategic pillars inside a six-pillar implementation frame ([strategy](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030), [launch](2026-03-16-mnangagwa-launches-five-year-ai-strategy), [penetration](2026-03-13-mavetera-84-55-internet-penetration-ai-strategy), [lessons](2026-05-22-cipesa-zimbabwe-ai-strategy-policy-lessons)).

A National AI Council is named in the strategy as the critical first step and remains planned ([council](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030)), and an implementation office is provided for in the ICT ministry, funded from the Treasury and the regulator-managed universal service fund ([office](2026-03-16-mnangagwa-launches-five-year-ai-strategy)).

The strategy carries its own account of its consultations, closing at a provincial centre in September 2025; that record is the strategy's account of itself ([consultations](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030)). Every institution the strategy creates is still planned.

summary: The [National ICT Policy 2022-2027](2022-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ict-policy-2022-2027) states no adoption or publication date anywhere in its text, and a [Smart Zimbabwe 2030 master plan](2019-01-01-smart-zimbabwe-2030-master-plan) carries no publication date, foreword date or gazette reference.
developments:
The ICT policy is the operative published national instrument, distinct from a still-unpublished 2026-2030 policy named in passing elsewhere; its year is padded from its own title ([policy](2022-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ict-policy-2022-2027)).

The master plan builds on a 2016-2020 policy and a continental manifesto, and its year is padded from its own end-2018 baseline data ([master plan](2019-01-01-smart-zimbabwe-2030-master-plan)).

Two undated national instruments, both dated here by inference from their own contents, is the documentary base under everything in this unit.

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence act](2026-03-16-ai-strategy-mandates-local-storage) is proposed by the strategy with no draft on record, and an [ethics framework](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) is committed for tabling by the first quarter of 2027.
developments:
The act is a strategy proposal with no draft on record ([act](2026-03-16-ai-strategy-mandates-local-storage), [privacy](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))).

The minister's own caveat on the ethics framework was that policy without implementation is mere poetry ([framework](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

A regulatory sandbox is named in the strategy and a supervising council was announced in August 2026 ([sandbox](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge)), and technical standards are likewise a strategy proposal ([standards](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))). Four artificial-intelligence instruments, all proposed by one strategy that has no legal force.

summary: A [National Data Agency](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) and a [national digital regulatory committee](2026-03-16-mnangagwa-launches-five-year-ai-strategy) are both provided for in the artificial-intelligence strategy, and both remain planned.
developments:
The data agency is provided for in the strategy approved by Cabinet in October 2025 ([agency](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030)).

The regulatory committee would report to the communications regulator, which is also the designated data protection authority ([committee](2026-03-16-mnangagwa-launches-five-year-ai-strategy)).

Creating a data agency and a regulatory committee under a body that already holds both the telecommunications and data-protection mandates is a concentration the strategy proposes and does not address.

summary: A [Postal and Telecommunications (Amendment) Bill](2025-10-10-zimbabwe-postal-and-telecommunications-amendment-bill-hb-10-2025) is before the Parliamentary Legal Committee, and a [local-ownership rule](2026-06-12-si-101-2026-postal-telecommunications-ownership-requirements-licences) was gazetted and reported repealed within weeks.
developments:
The bill was gazetted in October 2025 and reached the legal committee in August 2026; the Act it amends constitutes the communications regulator, which is also the designated data protection authority ([bill](2025-10-10-zimbabwe-postal-and-telecommunications-amendment-bill-hb-10-2025), [watch](2026-08-02-bill-watch-28-2026-of-2nd-august-2026)).

The ownership rule was gazetted on 12 June 2026 and reported repealed by a later statutory instrument; the repeal is reported and not verified against a primary, and no copy of the repealing instrument is held ([rule](2026-06-12-si-101-2026-postal-telecommunications-ownership-requirements-licences)).

A gazetted ownership requirement whose repeal cannot be verified is a live uncertainty for every licensee in the market.

summary: Cabinet directed drafting of a [statutory instrument on e-hailing services](2026-08-20-cite-zimbabwe-e-hailing-regulation-revenue), reported to Parliament in August 2026 with no text, consultation or commencement date published.
developments:
It is a drafting instruction ([direction](2026-08-20-cite-zimbabwe-e-hailing-regulation-revenue)).

It is the only platform-economy instrument in this ledger, and the revenue motive named in the reporting is what places it here rather than in transport.

summary: The [Cyber and Data Protection Act](2022-03-11-zimbabwe-cyber-and-data-protection-act-chapter-12-07) was consolidated in 2022, and [Statutory Instrument 155 of 2024](2024-09-13-zimbabwe-si-155-2024-licensing-data-controllers-dpo-regulations) created a data-controller licensing regime a legal expert calls new and strange.
developments:
The same Act establishes a cyber security centre and inserts a false-data-message offence into the criminal code ([Act](2022-03-11-zimbabwe-cyber-and-data-protection-act-chapter-12-07), [overview](2025-06-30 Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act - Overview)).

The statutory instrument was gazetted in September 2024 with licence applications due six months on; two outlets date the deadline to 12 March 2025 and the gazetted text's own reckoning gives 13 March, and an analyst expects the cost to reach consumers as dearer airtime and data ([instrument](2024-09-13-zimbabwe-si-155-2024-licensing-data-controllers-dpo-regulations), [warning](2026-03-27-potraz-warning-unlicensed-data-controllers), [fees](2026-07-30-potraz-data-licence-fees-slammed-as-costly-burden-on-businesses-and-consumers)).

Two regulatory notices followed in 2026, neither published by the regulator itself: the first is reported with no signature date held ([notice one](2026-03-27-potraz-warning-unlicensed-data-controllers)), and the second sets inspections beginning 1 September 2026 ([notice two](2026-07-28-zimbabwe-potraz-data-protection-inspections-1-september)).

progress: Mixed, a licensing and certification regime built out while its fees are objected to as a cost that reaches consumers
summary: [721 data controllers were licensed](2025-10-17-government-enforces-data-privacy-laws) by October 2025 with no figure since, [close to 1,200 officers trained](2026-05-14-potraz-plots-crackdown-data-act), and [certification costs US$1,250 plus a US$30 application fee](2026-07-28-zimbabwe-potraz-data-protection-inspections-1-september) per officer.
developments:
The licensed-controller count has not moved since October 2025 ([licensed](2025-10-17-government-enforces-data-privacy-laws), [institutions](2025-06-06-570-institutions-data-controller-licences)), and close to 1,200 officers have been trained ([trained](2026-05-14-potraz-plots-crackdown-data-act)).

Certification is required of every officer at US$1,250 plus a US$30 application fee ([certification](2026-07-28-zimbabwe-potraz-data-protection-inspections-1-september)). Doctors have objected to the levies, the statutory instrument's fee schedule is not held, and no licence count, exemption or regulator response to the objections is on record ([objections](2026-08-16-zimbabwe-doctors-data-protection-levies), [critique](2026-08-14-zimbabwe-data-protection-regulations-review-critique)).

Mandatory compliance inspections begin on 1 September 2026; the notice sets a start date and no inspection programme, sanction schedule or first action is published ([inspections](2026-08-17-postonsunday-potraz-september-data-protection-compliance-deadline), [crackdown](2026-05-14-potraz-plots-crackdown-data-act)).

summary: A [National Child Online Protection Policy 2026-2030](2026-08-12-zimbabwe-child-online-protection-policy-critique) was approved by Cabinet with the text not held, and the anti-corruption commission set out [investigations into cyber-enabled fraud in state digital systems](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-zacc-cyber-fraud-digital-systems-probe).
developments:
The policy text is not held, and no reporting route, responder training programme or budget line for it is on record ([policy](2026-08-12-zimbabwe-child-online-protection-policy-critique)); an earlier policy of the same name was reported established alongside the cybersecurity strategy on the minister's claim, relayed by one outlet ([earlier](2025-10-17-government-enforces-data-privacy-laws)).

The fraud figures are the commission chair's, given at a conference; no charge sheet, audit report or system-remediation record is held for any of the three systems ([investigations](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-zacc-cyber-fraud-digital-systems-probe)).

A privacy responsibility challenge was launched by the regulator, reaching the base at two-month date precision through a recurring round-up ([challenge](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))).

summary: A [cyber security and monitoring of interception centre](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information) sits as a unit in the Office of the President, and a [national truth-verification platform](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information) is proposed, layered on a false-data-message offence.
developments:
The centre was established by the Cyber and Data Protection Act, which amends the interception statute to create it; the Act's long title and the reporting organisation's account name the body differently ([centre](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information), [Act](2022-03-11-zimbabwe-cyber-and-data-protection-act-chapter-12-07)).

The truth-verification platform is proposed in the artificial-intelligence strategy and is layered on the false-data-message offence and that monitoring centre ([platform](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information)).

A state truth-verification platform proposed on top of an existing false-information offence and an interception unit in the presidency is the combination, and the strategy that proposes it has no legal force.

summary: A [three-day regional data-governance harmonisation workshop](2026-08-16-zimbabwe-sadc-harare-data-governance-workshop) was held in the capital, and a [bilateral immigration memorandum](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-rwanda-border-technology-obms-immigration) carried a benchmarking visit on border technology.
developments:
No outcome document, commitment or timetable from the workshop is held ([workshop](2026-08-16-zimbabwe-sadc-harare-data-governance-workshop)).

The immigration memorandum was signed in 2024 at year precision, its text not held, and a benchmarking visit followed in July 2026 ([memorandum](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-rwanda-border-technology-obms-immigration)).

The border system that visit examined is recorded separately, and its transfer to another state runs on that bilateral memorandum and study visits rather than a continental standard.

summary: Digital and information technology lines were [appropriated in the 2026 Appropriation Act](2025-12-29-zwe-2026-23-i), and no revised, released or actual figure is held.
developments:
These are original appropriations only, carried in local currency with no dollar equivalent stated ([appropriation](2025-12-29-zwe-2026-23-i), [second](2025-12-29-zwe-2026-23-ii), [revenue](2025-11-27-zwe-2026-zimra-automation)).

A citizens budget was published for the 2025 financial year ([citizens](2026-06-02-open-budget-survey-2025-zimbabwe-country-report)), and a parliamentary budget office was assessed in an external open budget survey round rather than by government ([office](2026-06-02-open-budget-survey-2025-zimbabwe-country-report)).

Original appropriations with no outturn, in a unit whose universal services fund publishes no balance either, is the whole of the domestic financing record.

summary: A [United Nations contract for ICT equipment](2026-08-10-zimbabwe-undp-ict-equipment-contract-award) was awarded in August 2026, and a [regional science and technology accelerator](2026-08-11-fcdo-sta-s-southern-africa-programme) is at expressions-of-interest stage.
developments:
The equipment record is a contract-award notice, so the amount is exact and the purpose is only "ICT equipment" — what it equips, and for whom, is not established ([contract](2026-08-10-zimbabwe-undp-ict-equipment-contract-award), [record](2026-08-10-undp-zwe-2026-ict-equipment)).

The accelerator's fund is resourced and the delivery consortium is not chosen, with no national allocation stated ([accelerator](2026-08-11-fcdo-sta-s-southern-africa-programme)).

A youth digital skills programme carries a SEK 36,000,000 commitment from 2023, converted in the record at a stated rate ([skills](2023-01-01-sida-zwe-plan-digital-skills-youth-2023-plan-international-digital-skills-4-youth)).

summary: A [scheme of reconstruction](2025-12-24-econet-notice-completion-infrastructure-restructuring) transferred passive infrastructure into a new company that [listed on the foreign-currency exchange](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers), while the [parent delisted voluntarily](2025-12-15-econet-wireless-zimbabwe-further-cautionary-announcement) citing a valuation discount.
developments:
The reconstruction completed in December 2025, with assets registered elsewhere held as nominee or in trust ([reconstruction](2025-12-24-econet-notice-completion-infrastructure-restructuring), [circular](2026-02-04-econet-wireless-zimbabwe-circular-and-econet-infraco-pre-listing-statement)).

The infrastructure company listed by introduction on the foreign-currency exchange in March 2026 ([listing](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers), [completion](2025-12-24-econet-notice-completion-infrastructure-restructuring), [statement](2026-02-04-econet-wireless-zimbabwe-circular-and-econet-infraco-pre-listing-statement)).

The parent's board resolved voluntary delisting in December 2025, citing a valuation discount against African peers ([delisting](2025-12-15-econet-wireless-zimbabwe-further-cautionary-announcement)). A syndicated vendor loan channelled US$300m of a US$500m group facility to the national operator in 2015, held as two records whose commitments cannot both be added ([loan](2015-01-01-cdb-zwe-001-china-development-bank-and-zte-corporation)).

summary: A [cross-border fibre public-private partnership](2026-07-06 Powertel, Paratus Zimbabwe switch on new digital highway) switched on its first phase, and [aviation and border-security digitisation talks](2026-08-08-zimbabwe-fujairah-digital-security-partnership) were held at State House.
developments:
The partnership is an equal-investment arrangement with the state operator retaining operational control ([partnership](2026-07-06 Powertel, Paratus Zimbabwe switch on new digital highway), [highway](2026-07-03-powertel-paratus-digital-highway)).

The border-security talks produced no instrument, value, scope or data-protection provision for systems that would process traveller data ([talks](2026-08-08-zimbabwe-fujairah-digital-security-partnership)).

A state operator keeping operational control in an equal-investment partnership is an unusual structure in this frame and is recorded as such.

summary: [Fifth-generation base stations](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026) rose on first-quarter 2026 sector data, and the state mobile operator's [turnaround plan](2026-07-15-netone-at-30-digital-future) restated a US$1bn-by-2029 target weeks before its chief executive was terminated.
developments:
The base-station and rural-coverage figures are the regulator's own ([stations](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026), [report](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025), [comparison](2026-04-30-econet-5g-exceeds-netone-telecel-combined)).

The turnaround target was restated at an annual general meeting; revenue figures are operator-reported and the same source states two growth rates that cannot both be right, and the chief executive's contract was terminated in August 2026 ([plan](2026-07-15-netone-at-30-digital-future), [termination](2026-08-04-netone-terminates-mushanawani-contract)).

Base stations deployed by the infrastructure company are company-reported for the quarter to May 2026 ([deployment](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers)), and a broadband mapping programme is working with operators to identify poor-coverage areas ([mapping](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout)).

progress: Mixed, a cross-border corridor switched on while ministerial fibre-length figures do not reconcile with each other or the regulator
summary: Two [ministerial fibre-length figures four months apart](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026) reconcile neither with each other nor with the regulator's series, and a [cross-border corridor](2026-07-06 Powertel, Paratus Zimbabwe switch on new digital highway) carries traffic on phase one.
developments:
Two ministerial figures four months apart and a regulator series that matches neither is the measurement position ([length](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026), [report](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025)).

The corridor's first phase runs on an indefeasible right-of-use model with the state operator retaining operational control ([corridor](2026-07-06 Powertel, Paratus Zimbabwe switch on new digital highway), [switch-on](2026-07-03-powertel-paratus-digital-highway)).

Government arrears owed to the state fixed operator doubled on the chief executive's statement at an annual general meeting; the two currency figures are the company's own ([arrears](2026-06-29-govt-debt-to-telone-doubles)) — the state is the largest debtor of the operator carrying its backbone.

summary: [Equipped international bandwidth](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025) rose on the regulator's fourth-quarter 2025 report, and the apparent collapse in headline used bandwidth is a [reclassification](2026-05-19-starlink-broke-potraz-bandwidth-framework) rather than a fall in traffic.
developments:
The measure excludes the satellite operator from the second quarter of 2025 ([bandwidth](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025)).

The satellite operator was excluded and the baseline restated from that quarter, so the apparent collapse in headline used bandwidth is a reclassification and not a fall in traffic ([framework](2026-05-19-starlink-broke-potraz-bandwidth-framework), [report](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025)).

Naming a measurement change as a measurement change is what stops a series break being read as a collapse. A terrestrial segment of a trans-continental cable, built by a domestically owned group, is stated ready for service in 2027 ([segment](2025-09-22 Google plans to build four subsea cable connectivity hubs for Africa)).

summary: A [national internet exchange point](2020-10-06-potraz-harare-regional-internet-exchange-point-itu-rdf-afr-2020) was reported to an international development forum in October 2020, and no traffic, peering or membership figure later than that is held.
developments:
The report was made in October 2020 ([exchange](2020-10-06-potraz-harare-regional-internet-exchange-point-itu-rdf-afr-2020)).

Six years without a traffic, peering or membership figure is the record. It matters against the international-bandwidth series, because domestic peering is what would keep local traffic off that link.

summary: [Internet penetration](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025) is active subscriptions divided by population rather than users, against a private tracker measuring 38.4 per cent of individuals, and [wireless became the majority fixed technology](2026-05-19-over-50pc-fixed-broadband-now-wireless).
developments:
The regulator's rate divides active subscriptions by population and is not a measure of individual use ([penetration](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025), [roadmap](2026-07-17-zimbabwe-digital-roadmap-msme-growth)).

Wireless became the majority fixed-broadband technology during the third quarter of 2025 ([mix](2026-05-19-over-50pc-fixed-broadband-now-wireless)), and internet and data traffic rose on first-quarter 2026 figures given at a post-Cabinet briefing ([traffic](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026)).

A preferential buyer's credit for fixed broadband expansion ended in 2019; its title states US$98.6m and its deal record carries US$110,675,991, with no conversion basis on either ([credit](2015-01-01-eximbank-cn-zwe-001-china-eximbank-provides-986-million-preferential)).

summary: [Satellite service launched in September 2024](2026-05-06-zimbabwe-starlink-vsat-record-potraz) after a cut-off order, [two licences were issued](2024-09-10-techzim-potraz-press-statement-licensing-of-starlink-575k) with no coverage obligation or duration stated, and [terminal subscriptions](2026-05-06-zimbabwe-starlink-vsat-record-potraz) are counted as a category rather than by operator.
developments:
The service launched in September 2024 after the 2024 cut-off order, and licence terms, fee and duration are not held ([service](2026-05-06-zimbabwe-starlink-vsat-record-potraz), [rural](2025-06-26-starlink-hype-cities-silence-rural)).

Two licences were issued in September 2024 and announced four days later; no coverage obligation, duration or universal-service term is stated in the held account ([licences](2024-09-10-techzim-potraz-press-statement-licensing-of-starlink-575k), [award](2024-09-10-techzim-potraz-press-statement-licensing-of-starlink-575k)).

The regulator counts satellite terminals as a category and not the operator separately ([terminals](2026-05-06-zimbabwe-starlink-vsat-record-potraz)), and the country's share of the African satellite market is reported off that same series ([share](2026-05-26 Africa risks losing billions to satellite internet operators, report says)); the state fixed operator's own satellite reseller revenue is reported in its 2025 annual report ([reseller](2026-06-29-govt-debt-to-telone-doubles)).

summary: An [uncapped 500 Mbps fibre package at US$99](2026-05-07-liquid-fibre-price-war-starlink) came out of a price war, while [satellite subscriptions grew](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout) against a rural population 76 per cent of whom live below the poverty line.
developments:
The package prices are the operators' own, quoted in United States dollars ([package](2026-05-07-liquid-fibre-price-war-starlink), [wireless](2026-05-19-over-50pc-fixed-broadband-now-wireless)).

Satellite subscriptions grew in scale only; affordability is unchanged against a rural population three-quarters of whom live below the poverty line ([affordability](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout), [silence](2025-06-26-starlink-hype-cities-silence-rural)).

A media institute's review of internet affordability against income was published in August 2026 on regulator data; it is a review rather than a household survey, and the penetration figure it uses counts active subscriptions ([review](2026-08-16-zimbabwe-internet-affordability-access-misa)).

summary: [Satellite kits at rural health facilities are not activated](2026-07-17-starlink-kits-gather-dust-rural-hospitals) because subscriptions are unpaid, on the health minister's own statement to the National Assembly.
developments:
The minister told the National Assembly the subscriptions are unpaid ([facilities](2026-07-17-starlink-kits-gather-dust-rural-hospitals)).

The donation programme handed out kits with no cumulative total published by government, and the health minister's account is that they are not activated ([kits](2026-07-17-starlink-kits-gather-dust-rural-hospitals), [donation](2025-07-24-govt-donates-250-starlink-kits-local-authorities), [record](2026-05-06-zimbabwe-starlink-vsat-record-potraz)).

Hardware distributed and left unconnected for want of a subscription line is the sharpest delivery failure in this unit, and it is stated by the responsible minister in Parliament.

summary: An operator [commissioned a 5 MW facility](2025-06-07-econet-data-centre-onboarding) in June 2025, which alone exceeds the [about 2 to 2.5 MW](2025-07-01-xalam-d4d-data-centre-market-brief-zimbabwe-2025) analysts put on the whole commercial estate three weeks later.
developments:
An operator commissioned a 5 MW data centre in Harare with a continental data-centre operator and began onboarding corporate clients at the end of June 2025, selling it on guaranteed power availability against load shedding and stating an intention to double it to 10 MW ([facility](2025-06-07-econet-data-centre-onboarding)).

The market estimates were commissioned by a European facility and the brief gives both about 2 MW and about 2.5 MW for the national live load ([capacity](2025-07-01-xalam-d4d-data-centre-market-brief-zimbabwe-2025)). One commissioned facility of 5 MW and a national estate of 2 MW measured three weeks apart cannot both be right, and nothing on file reconciles them.

The technology park's groundbreaking is expected in the fourth quarter of the financial year, with capacity, cost and completion date unstated throughout ([park](2026-07-21-econet-infraco-ai-telecom-infrastructure-vfex), [approval](2025-12-19 Econet approves ambitious Harare IT park data centre), [ai-ready](2026-01-14-zimbabwe-ai-ready-data-center-tech-park)).

The state operator's facility is described as a tier-three environment on its own undated product page, not certified or dated ([state facility](2026-08-08-telone-data-centre-and-cloud-services)).

summary: A [national high-performance computing centre](2017-01-01-china-mofcom-zwe-002-chinese-government-provides-rmb-100-million) took a CNY 100,000,000 phase-two grant in 2017 to raise capacity from 36 to over 300 teraflops, and no delivered figure is held.
developments:
Phase two was signed in December 2017 for implementation from 2018 ([centre](2017-01-01-china-mofcom-zwe-002-chinese-government-provides-rmb-100-million), [grant](2017-01-01-china-mofcom-zwe-002-chinese-government-provides-rmb-100-million)), after a phase-one interest-free loan that ended in 2015 ([phase one](2015-01-01-china-mofcom-zwe-001-chinese-government-provides-rmb-33-million)).

Both records carry dollar equivalents with no conversion date stated.

A university high-performance computer is operating with access quoted in large blocks rather than pay-as-you-go, developer-reported through one outlet rather than by the institution ([university](2026-04-17-econet-ai-launch-cassava-compute)). Nine years on from the capacity target, no delivered figure exists.

progress: Mixed, a sovereign cloud and local storage mandated by a strategy with no legal force while the operator's AI compute is sited abroad
summary: A [sovereign national cloud](2026-03-16-ai-strategy-mandates-local-storage) is provided for in a strategy a media rights organisation records as having no legal force, and the [operator states its artificial-intelligence compute is hosted abroad](2026-04-16-econet-launches-dedicated-ai-unit-to-drive-digital-transformation).
developments:
The strategy mandates local storage; a media rights organisation records that it has no legal force, and a proposed act is named as the instrument that would supply residency rules ([cloud](2026-03-16-ai-strategy-mandates-local-storage), [implications](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information)).

The operator's own launch announcement states first-hand that the compute is hosted in a neighbouring country ([siting](2026-04-16-econet-launches-dedicated-ai-unit-to-drive-digital-transformation), [service](2026-04-17-econet-ai-launch-cassava-compute), [unit](2026-04-16-econet-launches-dedicated-ai-unit-to-drive-digital-transformation)).

A residency mandate with no legal force, and the country's principal artificial-intelligence service running outside its borders on the provider's own statement, is the sovereignty position the record supports.

summary: Phase one of a [100 MW solar farm for the technology park](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers) began construction in the quarter to May 2026, on company-reported figures.
developments:
The construction start is company-reported ([solar farm](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers), [update](2026-07-21-econet-infraco-ai-telecom-infrastructure-vfex)).

A generation licence was issued to the mobile operator in March 2018; the capacity of the power arm now inside the infrastructure company is not held ([licence](2018-04-17-techzim-econet-willowvale-solar-generation-licence-gc0066-2018)).

Building generation for a data centre whose own capacity, cost and completion date are unstated is the sequence, and both halves are the company's own account.

summary: [Solar systems were deployed across new and existing tower sites](2026-07-21-econet-infraco-ai-telecom-infrastructure-vfex), [artificial-intelligence fuel management](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers) entered phased rollout, and [1,044 health facilities were solarised](2025-08-01-global-fund-zimbabwe-digital-health-case-study) across all ten provinces.
developments:
The tower solar deployment and the fuel-management rollout are both company-reported for the quarter to May 2026, and the fuel-management gain is unquantified ([solar](2026-07-21-econet-infraco-ai-telecom-infrastructure-vfex), [fuel](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers)).

The health solarisation figures are the health financing partner's own, covering 1,044 facilities across all ten provinces ([health](2025-08-01-global-fund-zimbabwe-digital-health-case-study)).

Solarising every province's health facilities while the satellite kits at rural health facilities sit unactivated for want of subscription payments is the contrast worth stating: the power arrived and the connectivity did not.

summary: A [National Cybersecurity Strategy](2025-10-17-government-enforces-data-privacy-laws) launched in October 2025, and an [incident response team project](2026-08-08-itu-project-9zim17008-zimbabwe-national-cirt-establishment) ran 2017 to 2021 with no completion recorded.
developments:
The strategy was launched in the capital in October 2025 ([strategy](2025-10-17-government-enforces-data-privacy-laws)).

The response team project ran from July 2017 to February 2021 with no completion recorded, and a first-party statement naming it is now held ([project](2026-08-08-itu-project-9zim17008-zimbabwe-national-cirt-establishment), [priorities](2025-01-01-zimbabwe-ministry-of-ict-priority-projects-national-data-centre)).

An artificial-intelligence and cybersecurity fusion centre is proposed in the strategy, which has no legal force ([fusion](2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information)). The central bank governor flags cyber risk in the payment system without sizing it: no incident count, loss figure or breach series accompanies the assessment, and its one hard number is that only 36 per cent of deployed terminals are active ([payments](2026-08-20-zimbabwe-flags-cyber-risks-in-digital-payments)).

summary: A [whole-of-government enterprise resource planning system](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) was launched as the precondition for clean public-sector data, and [open interface standards](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) are a ministerial commitment rather than a published standard.
developments:
The system was built by a domestic supplier and launched in July 2026; deployment coverage is not stated, and the ministry presents it as the precondition for clean public-sector data ([system](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

Mandated open interface standards for public-sector platforms are committed in the minister's five-point policy compass — a ministerial commitment, not a published standard ([standards](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

Government information technology specification standards reached version 2.0 in May 2025, issued by the Office of the President and Cabinet's technology unit rather than the ICT ministry ([specifications](2025-05-26-govt-reviews-ict-standards), [version](2025-05-01-zimbabwe-government-ict-specifications-standards-version-2)).

summary: A [health information exchange](2026-06-15-zimbabwe-core-fhir-implementation-guide) has a core implementation guide held as a continuous-build draft marked for demonstration and practice purposes only.
developments:
The guide is the health ministry's own continuous build at version 0.1.0, marked "content is for demonstration and practice purposes only"; the underlying exchange is reported by the financing partner rather than by the ministry ([guide](2026-06-15-zimbabwe-core-fhir-implementation-guide), [case study](2025-08-01-global-fund-zimbabwe-digital-health-case-study)).

A published interoperability specification carrying its own disclaimer that it is not for production use is a precise statement of where health interoperability stands here.

summary: An [online border management system](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-rwanda-border-technology-obms-immigration) has been in phased rollout since January 2025 after 2024 pilots, and its transfer to another state runs on a bilateral memorandum rather than a continental standard.
developments:
The rollout has been phased from January 2025 following biometric border-post pilots in 2024 ([system](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-rwanda-border-technology-obms-immigration), [pilots](2024-05-15 Zimbabwe implements biometric border posts for automating immigration processes)).

The transfer to another state runs on a 2024 bilateral memorandum and study visits, not a continental standard — which makes this an export of a system rather than adoption of one.

progress: Mixed, three million documents issued in a 2022 mobile exercise while the responsible minister says he is unaware of any backlog
summary: A [2022 mobile civil registration exercise issued 3,203,389 documents](2023-02-10-civil-registry-issues-over-3-million-identity-documents-for-free-ahead-of-july-elections), and the home affairs minister [said he was not aware of any identity-document backlog](2026-05-14-minister-denies-id-backlog) and was hearing of it for the first time.
developments:
The 2022 exercise ran February to September and was reported to Parliament by the home affairs minister ([exercise](2023-02-10-civil-registry-issues-over-3-million-identity-documents-for-free-ahead-of-july-elections)).

The backlog measure is set against that minister's denial in the Senate; he said he was not aware of any backlog and was hearing of it for the first time ([backlog](2026-05-14-minister-denies-id-backlog)).

A donor-funded mobile registration drive ran for five days in a remote district in July 2025 with no count of documents issued held ([drive](2025-07-14-bringing-identity-home-mobile-registration-binga)), and birth registration coverage is dated to the 2023-24 demographic and health survey rather than to the articles reporting it ([coverage](2025-07-10 Zimbabwe Launches Mobile ID Registration Program to Serve Remote Binga Communities)).

summary: A [national digital identity](2025-07-15 Zimbabwe looks forward to digital ID rollout after population registry reform) was announced in May 2025 for a July 2025 start with no start recorded, and every claim about it in the base is relayed second-hand.
developments:
No start is recorded and every claim is second-hand ([identity](2025-07-15 Zimbabwe looks forward to digital ID rollout after population registry reform), [denial](2026-05-14-minister-denies-id-backlog)).

Population registry modernisation began around 2023; the registrar-general states personnel are trained and materials in place, and no independent confirmation is held ([modernisation](2025-07-15 Zimbabwe looks forward to digital ID rollout after population registry reform)).

A digital identity announced fifteen months ago for a start that never happened, evidenced only at second hand, is the position — in a unit that has a licensing regime for data controllers and a certification fee for their officers.

summary: [Electronic passport enrolment](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-african-registrars-e-passport-civil-registration-model) runs in ten districts, eight provincial centres and one abroad, and [civil registration office computerisation](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-african-registrars-e-passport-civil-registration-model) bounds a decentralisation model three other states said they would copy.
developments:
The passport figures were stated by a deputy registrar general at a registrars' meeting ([passport](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-african-registrars-e-passport-civil-registration-model)).

The sub-office computerisation ratio bounds the decentralisation model three other states said they would copy, which is what makes the ratio worth stating ([computerisation](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-african-registrars-e-passport-civil-registration-model)).

A donor-funded programme to digitise and solarise civil registry sub-offices launched in August 2026 with no value, timetable, district list or birth-registration baseline against which to measure its effect ([sub-offices](2026-08-21-chinadaily-zimbabwe-gdssc-fund-civil-registry-digitisation), [digitisation](2026-08-08-zimbabwe-unicef-china-birth-registration-digitisation)).

summary: A [cotton farmer biometric registry](2025-10-10-nigeria-zimbabwe-farmer-digital-id) was cleared to proceed on the model of a [tobacco farmer identity registry](2025-10-10-nigeria-zimbabwe-farmer-digital-id) for which the base holds no primary.
developments:
The marketing authority was cleared to proceed with field teams stated for October 2025; that date is the acting chief executive's stated intention rather than a confirmed start ([cotton](2025-10-10-nigeria-zimbabwe-farmer-digital-id)).

The tobacco registry is cited as the model the cotton registry emulates, and the base holds no primary from the marketing board — only a secondary reference ([tobacco](2025-10-10-nigeria-zimbabwe-farmer-digital-id)).

Biometric registration of farmers by commodity marketing boards, modelled on a system nobody has published anything about, in a country with no working national digital identity.

A third farmer registry, run by a United Nations agency rather than a ministry, entered a second phase in October 2025 targeting 36,588 farmers across 12 districts in four provinces for the 2025/26 cropping season, with 14,915 registered by 30 October and completion expected in the first week of November ([farmer registry](2025-10-30-fao-digital-farmer-registry-zimbabwe)). Three separate farmer registries on three separate applications is the pattern worth naming: each is built for the programme that funded it.

summary: The central bank [established a digital transformation and financial technology department](2025-11-13-rbz-digital-transformation-fintech-department) with a sandbox and an innovation hub, and publishes a [quarterly national payment systems report](2026-07-01-rbz-national-payment-systems-report-second-quarter-2026).
developments:
The department was announced by a deputy governor at a technology forum; no separate central bank document is held ([department](2025-11-13-rbz-digital-transformation-fintech-department), [forum](2025-11-13-rbz-digital-transformation-fintech-department)).

The payment systems report is a first-party quarterly series; the first-quarter 2026 issue is not held, and the quarter-on-quarter comparison carried here is the second-quarter report's own ([report](2026-07-01-rbz-national-payment-systems-report-second-quarter-2026), [prior](2026-01-01-rbz-national-payment-systems-report-fourth-quarter-2025)).

Mobile money and interbank transfer limits were raised in the 2026 monetary policy statement, the bank stating the rise is intended to widen local-currency usage ([limits](2026-02-27-rbz-cuts-bank-charges-expands-zipit-limits)).

summary: [Bank charge caps](2026-02-27-rbz-cuts-bank-charges-expands-zipit-limits) were directed for compliance by March 2026, with a named analyst recording the governor conceding limited enforcement capacity.
developments:
The caps were set in the February 2026 monetary policy statement ([caps](2026-02-27-rbz-cuts-bank-charges-expands-zipit-limits), [consumer rights](2024-10-23 Electronic Transactions A Consumer Right - Consumer Protection Commission), [legal tender](2026-05-07-zig-legal-tender-why-cant-you-use-online)).

Online payment gateways are configured to settle in United States dollars first, so local currency is not accepted on them; that is named-analyst opinion, attributed ([gateways](2026-05-07-zig-legal-tender-why-cant-you-use-online)).

A price cap whose own setter concedes limited enforcement capacity, and a legal tender that online gateways will not take, are the two consumer findings this ledger supports.

progress: Mixed, electronic transaction value surging while cards issued far exceed cards in use
summary: [Electronic retail transaction value and volume](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey) rose in the first half of 2026 on figures in different currencies over different periods, and [cards issued far exceed cards in use](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey).
developments:
The two transaction figures are in different currencies over different periods and are not directly comparable ([transactions](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey), [growth](2025-09-15-digital-finance-sector-explosive-growth)).

The cards figure is a survey quoted by the researcher with no base, sample or method published ([cards](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey)), and national payment system value rose on June 2026 monthly figures, with the May volume derived from a reported fall rather than stated directly ([system value](2026-08-20-fingaz-zimbabwe-digital-payments-june-2026)).

A national financial inclusion strategy runs 2022 to 2026, citing formally served adults rising from 69 per cent in 2014 to 83 per cent in 2022 against a 90 per cent target ([inclusion](2022-01-01-rbz-zimbabwe-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-ii-2022-2026)).

summary: The [instant payment interchange](2024-01-01-siips-2024-zipit-zimbabwe-case-study) has run cross-domain transfers since 2011 across 17 commercial banks, and [interoperable code payments](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-electronic-transactions-top-zig1-trillion-zimswitch) are in rollout on the switch operator's report.
developments:
The interchange was established in 2011 by the payments association and the central bank against cash shortages, when non-cash payment ran on cash machines, terminals and cheques that took up to seven days to settle and mobile money did not yet exist in the country; it carries real-time credit-push transfers between bank accounts and mobile wallets across 17 commercial banks, person-to-person transfer remaining its most used case ([case study](2024-01-01-siips-2024-zipit-zimbabwe-case-study)).

The code-payment rollout is company-reported ([codes](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-electronic-transactions-top-zig1-trillion-zimswitch), [transactions](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey)).

Wallet cash-out onto bank machine estates has no launch dates in the source, so the analysis date is used ([cash-out](2026-07-02-o-mari-effect-mobile-money-war-cashout)). Ten cash-recycler machines are installed at retail outlets with 78 stated in the pipeline; the figures are the reporting outlet's rather than company-audited ([recyclers](2026-07-02-o-mari-effect-mobile-money-war-cashout)).

summary: [Participation in the continental payment and settlement system](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey) is company-reported to a payments conference, and [regional settlement onboarding](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking) is attributed to the operating central bank rather than to this one.
developments:
The continental participation reaches the base through the switch operator's report to a conference ([participation](2026-07-24-zimbabwe-digital-payments-surge-but-adoption-lags-topline-survey)).

The regional onboarding intent, cited as potentially by end-2027, is attributed to the operating central bank and nothing establishes a domestic decision ([onboarding](2026-07-29-sadc-rtgs-currencies-centralbanking)).

Card acceptance was extended to nine African markets with merchant and card counts given as the two companies' own and no country-specific figure ([cards](2026-08-19-tan-unionpay-standard-bank-nine-african-markets)).

summary: [Radio-frequency toll tag express lanes](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-widens-key-tollgates-as-e-toll-era-begins) opened at two of 29 plazas, with nothing stated on retention, access or legal basis for the movement record the tags generate.
developments:
The first plaza was handed over in July 2026 ([tolls](2026-07-29-zimbabwe-widens-key-tollgates-as-e-toll-era-begins)).

Nothing is stated on retention, access or legal basis for the movement record the tags generate — a vehicle-location dataset created by a revenue measure, in a unit with a licensing regime for data controllers that this system's operator would fall under.

A taxpayer registration self-service portal is readying a second phase of the wider revenue management system, integrating third-party stakeholders; that detail is paywalled beyond the free lede ([portal](2026-08-06-zimra-readies-tarms-phase-2-rollout)).

summary: A [digital capital-market venue](2026-07-31-zse-and-lloyd-corporate-capital-partner-to-unlock-growth-capital-for-zimbabwes-smes-through-zeex) was described as newly approved at the signing of a growth-capital memorandum, with no approval date for the venue itself stated.
developments:
The memorandum is an intent instrument and no approval date for the venue is stated ([venue](2026-07-31-zse-and-lloyd-corporate-capital-partner-to-unlock-growth-capital-for-zimbabwes-smes-through-zeex)).

A capital-market venue described as approved, at an event about something else, with no approval date, is the whole of the record.

summary: A [live cadastre portal](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-ecadastre-portal) carries property search and cadastral services, and a [two-week validation pilot](2026-04-07-title-deed-validation-reissuance-pilot-madzima) with sixteen law firms ended with no result on file.
developments:
The cadastre portal is live, carrying property search, electronic maps, cadastral and geodetic services and account registration, with surveyor modules behind a requested profile; the page carries no date of its own ([portal](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-ecadastre-portal)).

The instrument text on securitised deeds is not held; all three accounts of it are law-firm-authored and one firm has a commercial interest in validation volume ([instrument](2026-04-07-title-deed-validation-reissuance-pilot-madzima), [guide](2025-08-01 How to secure your property in Zimbabwe with the new digital deed system), [discussion](2025-07-28 Legal Discussions with Vengai Madzima - Digitization of the Deeds Registry in Zimbabwe)).

The pilot ran two weeks in April 2026 and is reported by one of the sixteen selected firms, with no result on file ([pilot](2026-04-07-title-deed-validation-reissuance-pilot-madzima)).

Naming the commercial interest of the only sources describing a deeds-validation regime is what a reader needs to weigh them. A public portal exists; what it has issued does not.

summary: A [third constitutional amendment on the voters roll](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-registrar-general-to-take-over-voters-roll) has begun implementation, [transferring the roll to the registrar-general](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-registrar-general-to-take-over-voters-roll) — the office that determines identity and vital status would also determine the electorate.
developments:
The justice minister told the Senate implementation had begun, with remaining work described as administrative rather than legislative ([amendment](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-registrar-general-to-take-over-voters-roll), [transfer](2026-07-23-zimbabwe-registrar-general-to-take-over-voters-roll)).

The office that determines identity and vital status would also determine the electorate. That is the finding, and the ledger states it directly rather than leaving it to inference.

It lands in a unit where the responsible minister says he is unaware of any identity-document backlog and where the national digital identity has never started.

progress: Mixed, national coverage unchanged and one province measured for the first time
summary: [1,254 of a planned 1,900 facilities](2025-08-01-global-fund-zimbabwe-digital-health-case-study) run the national electronic medical record, and [one province reports 90.2 per cent infrastructure coverage](2025-11-14-ehr-impilo-coverage-matabeleland-south) with a fifth of its sites not yet functional.
developments:
The facility figure is reported by the financing partner, and the platform's own page carries no publication or last-updated date ([record](2025-08-01-global-fund-zimbabwe-digital-health-case-study), [platform](2026-08-08-impilo-zimbabwe-national-health-operating-system)).

A provincial evaluation puts 90.2 per cent of that province's 153 facilities across seven districts on the record infrastructure with 110 sites fully functional, a functionality gap of 18.3 percentage points, and reports another province at 88 per cent coverage and 68 per cent functional ([evaluation](2025-11-14-ehr-impilo-coverage-matabeleland-south)).

The same evaluation records 15 facilities excluded from the rollout altogether — mine clinics, border posts and uniformed-forces facilities ([evaluation](2025-11-14-ehr-impilo-coverage-matabeleland-south)). Coverage is the number reported nationally; functionality is the number only one province has measured.

The health strategy's term ended in 2017 with no successor strategy held ([strategy](2012-01-01-zimbabwe-e-health-strategy-2012-2017)). An operator opened a virtual telemedicine hospital in one province, company-reported with no patient, consultation or availability figure ([telehealth](2026-07-15-netone-at-30-digital-future)).

summary: An [electronic procurement system](2025-09-10-praz-adopts-ai-egp-system) operational since January 2024 has added chatbots and machine-assisted bid evaluation, and there is still no national services portal in this ledger.
developments:
The procurement system was launched in October 2023 and became operational on 1 January 2024 for all public entities and bidders; the regulator says it has since added chatbots and virtual assistants and bid evaluation assisted by artificial intelligence, with no volume, saving or accuracy figure attached ([procurement](2025-09-10-praz-adopts-ai-egp-system)).

The denominator of local authorities is not given in the record held, so the share filing on time cannot be stated ([filing](2026-08-15-zimbabwe-zimra-digital-tax-councils-paperwork)).

The parliamentary programme is a first-hand account by the implementing partner with no national participant count ([programme](2026-07-28-idinsight-responsible-ai-african-parliaments)).

There is still no national services portal, service count or government online-service measure anywhere in this ledger, which is itself the finding for a unit of this size: the state has automated the buying and not the serving.

summary: One council's own page states its [billing runs on an enterprise resource planning package](2026-08-08-kwekwe-city-council-finance-department-billing-and-e-governance), not established as representative, and [250 satellite kits were handed to the local government ministry](2025-07-24-govt-donates-250-starlink-kits-local-authorities) with deployment falling to councils.
developments:
The closing position is one council's own statement and is not established as representative; no national follow-up audit of local-authority automation is held ([council](2026-08-08-kwekwe-city-council-finance-department-billing-and-e-governance), [audit](2025-06-18-zimbabwe-oag-local-authorities-report-2024)).

The reporting outlet notes deployment, maintenance and security of the satellite kits fall to councils, and no follow-up source is held ([kits](2025-07-24-govt-donates-250-starlink-kits-local-authorities)).

Kits handed to a ministry with the running costs pushed to councils is the same pattern the rural health facilities show, where the subscriptions were never paid.

summary: A [school connectivity and solar programme](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-school-connectivity-solar-starlink-target) targets every school connected by December 2026, on the minister's own counts with no school total or verification of working terminals stated.
developments:
The counts and the target are the minister's own; no school total, verification of installed and working terminals, or recurrent connectivity cost is stated ([programme](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-school-connectivity-solar-starlink-target)).

The recurrent cost is the point on which the rural health kits failed — hardware installed and subscriptions unpaid — and no source states who pays it for schools.

summary: The [universal services fund](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout) is vested in the regulator as trustee with [no balance or annual disbursement published](2025-06-16-auditor-general-zimbabwe-state-owned-enterprises-parastatals-2024) in the Auditor-General's 2024 report, and its [subscription support covers digital centres and schools](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) only.
developments:
Contribution rates are set by statutory instrument and the Auditor-General's 2024 report publishes no balance ([levy](2025-06-16-auditor-general-zimbabwe-state-owned-enterprises-parastatals-2024), [regulations](2021-01-08-zimbabwe-si-12-2021-postal-telecommunications-licensing-registration-certification-regulations), [amendment](2023-06-16-zimbabwe-si-110-2023-postal-telecommunications-postal-services-amendment-regulations-no-3), [scope](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout)).

Subscription support covers digital centres and schools, with a further unquantified share committed to artificial-intelligence projects ([support](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)) — which is the fund being asked to finance the artificial-intelligence strategy's institutions as well as connectivity.

A tower relocation programme is funded from the same fund ([towers](2026-05-16-govt-defends-starlink-rollout)), and rural network population coverage comes from the regulator's fourth-quarter 2025 report ([coverage](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025)).

summary: [409 free public wireless hotspots](2026-04-07 Zimbabwe switches on free wifi to power AI future) are deploying, and a [digital centres programme](2026-07-17-zimbabwe-digital-roadmap-msme-growth) is described as established nationwide offering free internet, equipment and literacy training.
developments:
The hotspot figure is ministry-reported ([hotspots](2026-04-07 Zimbabwe switches on free wifi to power AI future)).

The digital centres are described as established nationwide with no count, location list or usage figure ([centres](2026-07-17-zimbabwe-digital-roadmap-msme-growth), [kits](2026-07-17-starlink-kits-gather-dust-rural-hospitals)).

A presidential internet scheme is cited as the channel for satellite access with no site count published, and its start date is padded to 2025 because the source says only "earlier this year" ([scheme](2026-07-15-internet-traffic-surges-57pc-q1-2026)).

summary: A [nationwide expansion of artificial-intelligence traffic cameras](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-ai-traffic-cameras-national-rollout) was announced under a smart policing programme, and a separate [municipal traffic system](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-harare-ai-traffic-cameras-entrapment-concerns) is rolling out across the capital's central business district amid entrapment concerns.
developments:
The national rollout's supporting figure — an annual crash cost — is the transport ministry's, given in support of the rollout ([national](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-ai-traffic-cameras-national-rollout)).

The municipal system is distinct from the national police programme and is reported alongside entrapment concerns ([municipal](2026-08-07-zimbabwe-harare-ai-traffic-cameras-entrapment-concerns)).

An earlier capital traffic management system is reported in operation and described as developed by the state operator, with every claim in the source relayed second-hand ([earlier](2025-07-15 Zimbabwe looks forward to digital ID rollout after population registry reform)). Three overlapping camera programmes, none with a stated retention rule or legal basis.

summary: An [indigenous-language corpora programme](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) is committed with universities to lead and part-financing from the universal services fund, and an [artificial-intelligence literacy campaign](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) is introduced in the strategy.
developments:
The corpora programme is committed with universities leading and part-financed from the universal services fund ([corpora](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

The literacy campaign is introduced in the strategy ([campaign](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030)).

Both draw on a fund whose balance is unpublished and whose Auditor-General report gives no disbursement figure, which is the constraint under every artificial-intelligence commitment in this unit.

summary: [Artificial-intelligence remote monitoring and a digital twin](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers) are described as advancing in a company trading update for the quarter ended May 2026.
developments:
It is company-reported ([monitoring](2026-07-21-infraco-expands-ai-powered-towers)).

A digital twin of a tower estate is the most technically specific artificial-intelligence deployment claim in this unit, and it is a listed company's own trading-update language with no measure attached.

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence innovation fund](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) is named in the strategy and a separate catalyst fund was announced in August 2026, and the two are not stated to be the same vehicle.
developments:
The strategy names one fund and a catalyst fund was announced at a grand challenge launch; the two are not stated to be the same vehicle ([fund](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030), [catalyst](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge), [launch](2026-03-13-mavetera-84-55-internet-penetration-ai-strategy)).

A ring-fenced share of the universal services fund is committed for public-good artificial intelligence with no amount stated ([ring-fenced](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

The central bank cites a regulatory sandbox as operating, pre-dating the window with no earlier position held ([sandbox](2025-11-13-rbz-digital-transformation-fintech-department)), and an innovation hub was announced as to be created under the new department ([hub](2025-11-13-rbz-digital-transformation-fintech-department)).

summary: An [artificial-intelligence grand challenge](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge) launched in August 2026, and a [digital skills programme targeting 1.5 million people](2026-07-17-zimbabwe-digital-roadmap-msme-growth) is described as delivered with a Gulf state.
developments:
The challenge's own account gives about 60 participants against 68 projects reported, which does not reconcile and is unestablished ([challenge](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge), [progress](2026-08-02-mavetera-urges-ai-solutions-that-benefit-communities-as-nyanga-challenge-progresses), [strategy](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030)).

The 1.5 million target is described as delivered in partnership with a Gulf state ([skills](2026-07-17-zimbabwe-digital-roadmap-msme-growth)).

More than 3,000 youths were trained under a government cybersecurity programme ([cyber](2026-04-07 Zimbabwe switches on free wifi to power AI future)), and a digital skills ambassadors programme was named at the strategy launch ([ambassadors](2026-03-13-mavetera-84-55-internet-penetration-ai-strategy)).

summary: [Coding in the secondary curriculum](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold) was directed at a national seminar on digital sovereignty, and a [coding programme with a Gulf state](2026-04-07 Zimbabwe switches on free wifi to power AI future) rests on one excerpt source.
developments:
The curriculum direction was given at a seminar in July 2026 ([curriculum](2026-07-30-zimbabwe-ndarama-launch-ai-sovereignty-digital-gold)).

The Gulf attribution rests on one excerpt source, and a July 2026 restatement of the target does not name the partner ([programme](2026-04-07 Zimbabwe switches on free wifi to power AI future)).

A curriculum change directed by ministerial statement, and a delivery partnership whose partner cannot be confirmed, is the school-level record.

summary: The research council's [2023 and 2024 annual reports both confirm no gross research and development expenditure figure is published](2023-01-01-research-council-of-zimbabwe-annual-report-2023).
developments:
The absence is stated by the council's own annual reports, which is what makes it a finding rather than a gap in capture ([2023](2023-01-01-research-council-of-zimbabwe-annual-report-2023), [2024](2024-01-01-research-council-of-zimbabwe-annual-report-2024)).

No research and development expenditure figure, and no share of gross domestic product, exists for this country in either report. Against an artificial-intelligence strategy proposing four institutions and a corpora programme led by universities, the country's own research council publishes no measure of what it spends on research.

summary: An [ICT access and use survey](2026-07-20-zw-mobile-internet-survey) released its 2025 round on 9,245 households at 91.3 per cent response, and only one outlet's account of it is held rather than the report.
developments:
Only one outlet's account is held, not the report itself ([survey](2026-07-20-zw-mobile-internet-survey)).

Household internet access rose and household computer ownership fell on that survey; the ownership measure is five years apart and the intervening trend is not held ([access](2026-07-20-zw-mobile-internet-survey), [ownership](2026-07-20-zw-mobile-internet-survey)).

A household budget survey ran a nationwide listing exercise in August 2026 with no stated field or release date ([budget survey](2026-08-06-zimbabwe-zimstat-household-survey-preparations)), and the regulator's quarterly sector report bears no date on its face, the held copy being a rehost with a proxy publication date ([sector report](2026-04-29-potraz-abridged-sector-performance-report-q4-2025)).

summary: The statistics agency runs a [second version of its open data portal](2025-01-01-zimstat-odp2-tutorial-guide), while the strategy's own [data platform](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030) and a [data commons](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge) remain announcements.
developments:
A second version of the statistics agency's open data portal is in use, with an openly published sustainable development goals portal launched on 9 July 2025 and an access and tutorial guide issued for it ([guide](2025-01-01-zimstat-odp2-tutorial-guide)). The guide mixes several dates and carries none of its own, and no dataset count, download figure or licence statement is held.

The artificial-intelligence data platform is provided for in the strategy and is to be introduced gradually ([platform](2026-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ai-strategy-2026-2030), [launch](2026-03-16-mnangagwa-launches-five-year-ai-strategy)).

The data commons was announced in August 2026 ([commons](2026-08-04-zimbabwe-bets-on-ai-innovation-as-government-launches-national-grand-challenge)).

Neither announced instrument carries a dataset, custodian, licence or access rule. What is actually open is one agency's portal; what is promised is a platform and a commons under a strategy with no legal force.

summary: A [national geospatial and earth-observation agency](2019-03-29-zimbabwe-gn-483-2019-establishment-of-zingsa) was established by general notice in 2019, constituted as a research institute.
developments:
It was established by general notice in March 2019 ([agency](2019-03-29-zimbabwe-gn-483-2019-establishment-of-zingsa)).

No programme, dataset, budget or output is held for it at any date. Seven years of an earth-observation agency with nothing published about what it produces.

summary: The country [withdrew from bilateral health cooperation talks](2026-02-25-ap-us-zimbabwe-health-funding-talks-collapse) citing sovereignty, and the two figures for the offer are unclosable because both are the same party's statements about an unsigned instrument.
developments:
Withdrawal followed a presidential memo of December 2025; the model instruments were resolved in August 2026 and the gap between the two stated values is unclosable because both figures are the same party's statements about an unsigned offer ([withdrawal](2026-02-25-ap-us-zimbabwe-health-funding-talks-collapse), [sovereignty](2026-02-25 Zimbabwe Turns Down U.S. Health Funding, Citing Sovereignty Concerns), [model](2025-11-15-bass-afghs-model-data-sharing-agreement-25-year-access), [dispute](2026-08-04-newzimbabwe-us-embassy-disputes-account-365m-health-deal), [fact-check](2026-08-06-newshawks-us-fact-checks-zimbabwe-health-deal-account)).

A cloud partner experience centre opened at a summit; the facility is in a neighbouring country and the domestic interest is ownership rather than siting ([centre](2026-06-30-masiyiwa-manyika-google-1b-africa-cloud)).

Two countries in this frame declined the same health arrangement over its data terms, which makes it a pattern rather than an incident.

summary: The [national data centre](2026-03-01-data-sovereignty-in-africa-steering-digital-transformation-between-china-and-the-west) was launched in February 2021 under a US$98m broadband initiative, vendor-led and export-credit financed, and [city surveillance systems](2026-04-04 Chinese surveillance rolled out in Africa ZTE, Hikvision, Huawei at the helm) are mapped here with no domestic contract value or camera count held.
developments:
The data centre's date and figure come from a peer-reviewed article rather than a government statement ([centre](2026-03-01-data-sovereignty-in-africa-steering-digital-transformation-between-china-and-the-west)).

The surveillance mapping covers eleven countries and no domestic contract value or camera count is held ([surveillance](2026-04-04 Chinese surveillance rolled out in Africa ZTE, Hikvision, Huawei at the helm), [smart city](2026-03-01 Smart City Surveillance in Africa (IDS 2026))).

An export credit facility of CNY 485,000,000 for mobile network expansion was committed in 2019 with a dollar equivalent carrying no conversion date ([credit](2019-01-01-eximbank-cn-zwe-002-china-eximbank-provides-rmb-485-million)), and a forum in August 2026 discussed technology transfer critically, naming no project, transfer arrangement or commitment ([forum](2026-08-20-harare-forum-zimbabwe-china-africa-technology-transfer-critique)).

summary: The [multiannual indicative programme for 2021-2027](2022-03-08-eu-multiannual-indicative-programme-2021-2027-zimbabwe-annex) carries no digital priority area, and no country-specific artificial-intelligence or adequacy instrument is held.
developments:
The programme was adopted under a Commission implementing decision and has no digital priority area ([programme](2022-03-08-eu-multiannual-indicative-programme-2021-2027-zimbabwe-annex)).

No domestic artificial-intelligence or adequacy instrument with the bloc is held at any date. The only European involvement in this ledger is a commissioned data-centre market brief and an accelerator at expressions-of-interest stage.

summary: The revenue system reached [full implementation](2024-09-27-zimra-public-notice-73-tarms-release-3-go-live) in October 2024, and fiscalised transaction recording was extended to fuel in May 2026.
developments:
The tax and revenue management system reached full implementation with a five-module release on 1 October 2024, adding revenue forecasting, case management, extended debt management, investigations and audit, and risk management and compliance, with taxpayer-facing services through a self-service portal ([notice](2024-09-27-zimra-public-notice-73-tarms-release-3-go-live)).

It is integrated with the fiscalisation device management system, and a second phase integrating third-party stakeholders is being readied ([system](2026-08-06-zimra-readies-tarms-phase-2-rollout)).

Statutory Instrument 88 of 2026 extends fiscalised recording into fuel, requiring registration and providing for the procurement, approval and licensing of fuel fiscal device suppliers and developers ([regulations](2026-05-15-zimbabwe-si-88-2026-fuel-fiscal-devices)).

No transaction volume, revenue attribution or system availability figure is published for any of it.

summary: All superior courts are [paperless](2026-01-12-zimbabwe-cj-address-2026-legal-year) under the electronic case management system, and the magistrates' courts rollout reached its fourth phase in 2026.
developments:
The chief justice told the opening of the 2026 legal year that all superior courts are paperless under the Integrated Electronic Case Management System and that four magisterial provinces had been digitised under its fourth phase, with Manicaland and Mashonaland East to be prepared next ([address](2026-01-12-zimbabwe-cj-address-2026-legal-year)).

Sixteen magistrates' courts in Masvingo and Matabeleland South went live under phase 4.2 from October 2025, and the system reached the rural districts of Chipinge and Chimanimani on 13 January 2026 ([phase 4.2](2025-10-01-zimbabwe-iecms-phase-4-2-masvingo), [rural districts](2026-01-22-zwe-iecms-rural-electronic-court-system)).

Sixteen further magistrates' courts in Manicaland and Mashonaland East were set for digitisation under phase 4.3 from 1 June 2026 ([phase 4.3](2026-05-29-zimbabwe-iecms-phase-4-3-manicaland)).

Policing is the part of the justice chain that has not moved: an electronic docket system announced in December 2025 still carries no timetable, cost or supplier. No case volume or disposal-time figure from the court system is published.

summary: The [social registry](2026-02-17-zimbabwe-social-registry-support-project-pid) completed first-phase enumeration in December 2025 and has a funded second phase aiming at a further 4 per cent of the population.
developments:
The first phase of enumeration was completed in Mangwe district in December 2025 and extends to Nkayi and Mudzi, aiming at about 2 per cent of the population, roughly 80,000 households ([project document](2026-02-17-zimbabwe-social-registry-support-project-pid)).

A proposed second phase would enumerate at least a further 4 per cent, about 160,000 households, with US$1.7m for enumeration and US$300,000 for IT and capacity building ([project document](2026-02-17-zimbabwe-social-registry-support-project-pid)).

Field collection began publicly in Nkayi district in March 2026, gathering demographics, education, employment, housing, land ownership, access to services and economic activity ([launch](2026-03-14-zimbabwe-social-registry-survey-nkayi-rollout), [survey](2025-01-01-zimstat-2025-social-registry-survey-press-release)).

No enrolled-household count, hosting arrangement or completion date is held, and the registry has not yet carried a live targeting decision.

summary: The deadline for re-registering onto the [electronic registry](2026-04-17-zimbabwe-si-76-2026-business-re-registration-amendment) was moved out two years in April 2026, from 20 April 2026 to 20 April 2028.
developments:
The Companies and Other Business Entities Act constitutes the registration office under a chief registrar and defines the electronic registry and electronic records the register runs on ([Act](2019-11-15-zimbabwe-companies-other-business-entities-act)).

Statutory Instrument 108 of 2025 set 20 April 2026 as the deadline for companies and private business corporations registered before the electronic registry to re-register, with automatic deregistration and removal from the register for those that did not ([regulations](2025-09-26-zimbabwe-si-108-2025-business-re-registration)).

Three days before it fell due, Statutory Instrument 76 of 2026 deleted that date and substituted 20 April 2028 ([amendment](2026-04-17-zimbabwe-si-76-2026-business-re-registration-amendment)).

No count of entities re-registered, or still to re-register, is published at either date. Separately, of 204,798 establishments surveyed, more than 76 per cent were found operating informally ([establishments](2025-07-24-zimbabwenow-76-percent-businesses-unregistered)).

summary: Rural electricity access stands at [8 per cent](2025-01-22-zwe-zdhs-2023-24) against 67 per cent urban, and the energy minister has directed that every school and rural health centre be electrified by the end of 2026.
developments:
The 2023-24 demographic and health survey puts access to electricity at 8 per cent of the rural population against 67 per cent in urban areas ([survey](2025-01-22-zwe-zdhs-2023-24)).

The 2025 round of switch-on ceremonies closed on 31 October across eight rural provinces, with grid extension commissioned at sites in Binga, Insiza, Marondera, Muzarabani, Shurugwi, Gutu, Nyanga and Kariba districts reaching business centres, clinics and schools; the energy minister directed the agency to electrify every school and rural health centre in the country by the end of 2026 ([ceremonies](2025-10-31-zwe-rea-switch-on-ceremonies-2025)).

A 120 kW solar mini-grid was commissioned in Hurungwe district on 21 May 2026 by the rural electrification agency under the rural electrification fund with United Nations development support ([mini-grid](2026-05-27-undp-dete-solar-mini-grid)).

No count of connections made in the year is published, so the end-2026 direction cannot be measured against progress towards it.

summary: [National Development Strategy 2](2025-12-08-president-mnangagwa-launches-nds2) was launched in December 2025 for 2026 to 2030, and Cabinet names it with three standing instruments as the digital agenda's frame.
developments:
NDS2 was launched on 8 December 2025 as the successor national plan for 2026 to 2030, presented as the outcome of broad-based national consultations taking in the private sector, faith-based organisations, development partners and the diaspora ([launch](2025-12-08-president-mnangagwa-launches-nds2), [strategy](2025-11-27-zimbabwe-national-development-strategy-2-2026-2030)).

Cabinet's briefing of 14 July 2026 names NDS2, the Smart Zimbabwe 2030 master plan, the National ICT Policy and the National AI Strategy 2026-2030 as the frameworks the digital transformation agenda runs under ([briefing](2026-07-14-zimbabwe-cabinet-23rd-press-briefing)).

The base holds no single whole-of-government digital transformation strategy. The agenda is carried by four documents of different vintages, two of which state no adoption date of their own ([ICT policy](2022-01-01-zimbabwe-national-ict-policy-2022-2027), [master plan](2019-01-01-smart-zimbabwe-2030-master-plan)).

summary: A government [enterprise architecture blueprint](2026-05-08-zwe-mavetera-enterprise-architecture-linkedin) was handed over in May 2026 and a service bus announced; no interoperability framework document is held.
developments:
A customised government enterprise-architecture framework, strategy, roadmap and change-management plan was built over September 2023 to September 2024, with representatives of more than 40 ministries, departments and agencies taking part ([project](2024-01-01-enterprise-architecture-modelling-zimbabwe)).

The blueprint was handed over to government ICT directors in May 2026, and the ICT minister put radical interoperability first among five priorities, announcing a government service bus and an integrated online portal for once-only data sharing ([handover](2026-05-08-zwe-mavetera-enterprise-architecture-linkedin), [priorities](2026-05-08-zimbabwe-smart-government-digital-blueprint)).

A National Migration Data Strategy 2025-2030 was launched on 15 May 2026 with the migration agency and the statistics agency, a sector data-sharing framework rather than a national one ([migration data](2026-05-15-zimbabwe-national-migration-data-strategy-launch)).

No published interoperability framework, data-exchange specification or service-bus procurement is held.

summary: [Guideline CDPG 4](2025-01-01-potraz-data-protection-implementation-guidelines) bars hosting core banking and critical financial systems outside Zimbabwe without written approval, and enforcement becomes mandatory inspection in September 2026.
developments:
The data protection authority's implementation guidelines state that it will not permit the migration or hosting of highly sensitive information, such as core banking platforms and critical financial systems, outside Zimbabwe, and that any exception needs prior written approval on a risk assessment and justification ([guidelines](2025-01-01-potraz-data-protection-implementation-guidelines)).

Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 moves compliance from licensing to mandatory risk-based inspections of data controllers from 1 September 2026, beginning with nine priority sectors ([inspections](2026-08-12-potraz-mandatory-compliance-inspections)).
